scope: Pinned native rule-like units; no scenario coverage judgments.

tools.name: Headlamp diagnostics

rules.title: container start
rules.summary: Explains that a container could not start and directs investigation to its command, entrypoint, and image.

rules.title: containers not ready
rules.summary: Explains that one or more containers are not ready and directs investigation to container states and readiness probes.

rules.title: crashloop
rules.summary: Explains repeated post-start container crashes and directs investigation to logs and the previous exit code.

rules.title: evicted
rules.summary: Explains Pod eviction from node resource pressure and directs investigation to node conditions and resource requests and limits.

rules.title: image pull
rules.summary: Explains image retrieval failure and directs investigation to the image reference, registry reachability, and credentials.

rules.title: invalid config reference
rules.summary: Explains invalid container configuration commonly caused by a missing ConfigMap or Secret reference.

rules.title: oom killed
rules.summary: Explains termination after exceeding the memory limit and suggests checking memory usage and limits.

rules.title: unschedulable
rules.summary: Explains that the scheduler could not place the Pod and points to resources, taints, tolerations, and affinity.

tools.extraction_method: Manually enumerated reason branches in diagnosisHint.
tools.inventory_caveat: Eight explanation branches, not the complete Pod/workload finding surface.

rules.title: Alertmanager Cluster Crashlooping
rules.summary: Half or more of the Alertmanager instances within the same cluster are crashlooping.

rules.title: Alertmanager Cluster Down
rules.summary: Half or more of the Alertmanager instances within the same cluster are down.

rules.title: Alertmanager Cluster Failed To Send Alerts
rules.summary: All instances failed to send notification to an integration.

rules.title: Alertmanager ConfigInconsistent
rules.summary: The configuration between instances inside a cluster is inconsistent.

rules.title: Alertmanager Failed Reload
rules.summary: The alert AlertmanagerFailedReload is triggered when the Alertmanager instance for the cluster monitoring stack has consistently failed to reload its configuration for a certain period.

rules.title: Alertmanager Failed To Send Alerts
rules.summary: At least one instance is unable to routed alert to the corresponding integration.

rules.title: Alertmanager Members Inconsistent
rules.summary: At least one of alertmanager cluster members cannot be found.

rules.title: Config Reloader Sidecar Errors
rules.summary: Errors encountered while the config-reloader sidecar attempts to sync configuration in a given namespace.

rules.title: CPU Throttling High
rules.summary: Processes experience elevated CPU throttling.

rules.title: etcdBackendQuotaLowSpace
rules.summary: This alert fires when the total existing DB size exceeds 95% of the maximum DB quota. The consumed space is in Prometheus represented by the metric etcdmvccdbtotalsizeinbytes, and the DB quota size is defined by etcdserverquotabackendbytes.

rules.title: etcdGRPCRequestsSlow
rules.summary: This alert fires when the 99th percentile of etcd gRPC requests are too slow.

rules.title: etcdHighFsyncDurations
rules.summary: This alert fires when the 99th percentile of etcd disk fsync duration is too high for 10 minutes. Full context Every write request sent to etcd has to be [fsync'd][fsync] to disk by the leader node, transmitted to its peers, and fsync'd to those disks as well before etcd can tell the client that…

rules.title: etcdHighNumberOfFailedGRPCRequests
rules.summary: This alert fires when at least 5% of etcd gRPC requests failed in the past 10 minutes.

rules.title: etcdInsufficientMembers
rules.summary: This alert fires when there are fewer instances available than are needed by etcd to be healthy. This means that etcd cluster has not enough members in the cluster to create quorum.

rules.title: etcdMembersDown
rules.summary: This alert fires when one or more etcd member goes down and evaluates the number of etcd members that are currently down. Often, this alert was observed as part of a cluster upgrade when a master node is being upgraded and requires a reboot.

rules.title: etcdNoLeader
rules.summary: This alert is triggered when etcd cluster does not have a leader for more than 1 minute. This can happen if nodes from the cluster are orphaned - they were part of the cluster but now they are in minority and thus can not form a cluster, for example due to network partition.

rules.title: Info Inhibitor
rules.summary: This is an alert that is used to inhibit info alerts. By themselves, the info-level alerts are sometimes very noisy, but they are relevant when combined with other alerts. Full context More information about the alert and design considerations can be found in a kube-prometheus issue

rules.title: Kube Aggregated API Down
rules.summary: Kubernetes aggregated API has reported errors. It has appeared unavailable X times averaged over the past 10m.

rules.title: Kube Aggregated API Errors
rules.summary: Kubernetes aggregated API has reported errors. It has appeared unavailable over 4 times averaged over the past 10m.

rules.title: Kube API Down
rules.summary: The KubeAPIDown alert is triggered when all Kubernetes API servers have not been reachable by the monitoring system for more than 15 minutes.

rules.title: Kube API Error Budget Burn
rules.summary: Runbook guidance for Kube API Error Budget Burn.

rules.title: Kube API Terminated Requests
rules.summary: The apiserver has terminated over 20% of its incoming requests.

rules.title: Kube Client Certificate Expiration
rules.summary: A client certificate used to authenticate to the apiserver is expiring in less than 7 days (warning alert) or 24 hours (critical alert).

rules.title: Kube Client Errors
rules.summary: Kubernetes API server client is experiencing over 1% error rate in the last 15 minutes.

rules.title: Kube Container Waiting
rules.summary: Container in pod is in Waiting state for too long.

rules.title: Kube Controller Manager Down
rules.summary: KubeControllerManager has disappeared from Prometheus target discovery.

rules.title: Kube CPU Overcommit
rules.summary: Cluster has overcommitted CPU resource requests for Pods and cannot tolerate node failure. Full context Total number of CPU requests for pods exceeds cluster capacity. In case of node failure some pods will not fit in the remaining nodes.

rules.title: Kube CPU Quota Overcommit
rules.summary: Cluster has overcommitted CPU resource requests for Namespaces and cannot tolerate node failure.

rules.title: Kube DaemonSet MisScheduled
rules.summary: A number of pods of daemonset are running where they are not supposed to run.

rules.title: Kube DaemonSet Not Scheduled
rules.summary: A number of pods of daemonset are not scheduled.

rules.title: Kube DaemonSet Rollout Stuck
rules.summary: DaemonSet update is stuck waiting for replaced pod.

rules.title: Kube Deployment Generation Mismatch
rules.summary: Deployment generation mismatch due to possible roll-back.

rules.title: Kube Deployment Replicas Mismatch
rules.summary: Deployment has not matched the expected number of replicas. Full context Kubernetes Deployment resource does not have number of replicas which were declared to be in operation. For example deployment is expected to have 3 replicas, but it has less than that for a noticeable period of time. In…

rules.title: Kube HPA Maxed Out
rules.summary: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler has been running at max replicas for longer than 15 minutes.

rules.title: Kube HPA Replicas Mismatch
rules.summary: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler has not matched the desired number of replicas for longer than 15 minutes.

rules.title: Kube Job Completion
rules.summary: Job is taking more than 1h to complete.

rules.title: Kube Job Failed
rules.summary: Job failed complete.

rules.title: Kube Memory Overcommit
rules.summary: Cluster has overcommitted Memory resource requests for Pods and cannot tolerate node failure. Full context Total number of Memory requests for pods exceeds cluster capacity. In case of node failure some pods will not fit in the remaining nodes.

rules.title: Kube Memory Quota Overcommit
rules.summary: Cluster has overcommitted memory resource requests for Namespaces.

rules.title: Kube Node Not Ready
rules.summary: KubeNodeNotReady alert is fired when a Kubernetes node is not in Ready state for a certain period. In this case, the node is not able to host any new pods as described [here][KubeNode].

rules.title: Kube Node Readiness Flapping
rules.summary: The readiness status of node has changed few times in the last 15 minutes.

rules.title: Kube Node Unreachable
rules.summary: Kubernetes node is unreachable and some workloads may be rescheduled.

rules.title: Kube Persistent Volume Errors
rules.summary: PersistentVolume is having issues with provisioning.

rules.title: Kube Persistent Volume Filling Up
rules.summary: There can be various reasons why a volume is filling up. This runbook does not cover application specific reasons, only mitigations for volumes that are legitimately filling. As always refer to recommended scenarios for given service.

rules.title: Kube Pod Crash Looping
rules.summary: Pod is in CrashLoop which means the app dies or is unresponsive and kubernetes tries to restart it automatically.

rules.title: Kube Pod Not Ready
rules.summary: Pod has been in a non-ready state for more than 15 minutes. State Running but not ready means readiness probe fails. State Pending means pod can not be created for specific namespace and node. Full context Pod failed to reach ready state, depending on the readiness/liveness probes. See pod-lifecycle

rules.title: Kube Quota Almost Full
rules.summary: Cluster reaches to the allowed limits for given namespace.

rules.title: Kube Quota Exceeded
rules.summary: Cluster reaches to the allowed hard limits for given namespace.

rules.title: Kube Quota Fully Used
rules.summary: Cluster reached allowed limits for given namespace.

rules.title: Kube Scheduler Down
rules.summary: Kube Scheduler has disappeared from Prometheus target discovery.

rules.title: Kube State Metric sWatch Errors
rules.summary: kube-state-metrics is experiencing errors in watch operations.

rules.title: Kube State Metrics List Errors
rules.summary: kube-state-metrics is experiencing errors in list operations.

rules.title: Kube State Metrics Sharding Mismatch
rules.summary: kube-state-metrics sharding is misconfigured.

rules.title: Kube State Metrics Shards Missing
rules.summary: kube-state-metrics shards are missing.

rules.title: Kube StatefulSet Generation Mismatch
rules.summary: StatefulSet generation mismatch due to possible roll-back.

rules.title: Kube StatefulSet Replicas Mismatch
rules.summary: StatefulSet has not matched the expected number of replicas. Full context Kubernetes StatefulSet resource does not have number of replicas which were declared to be in operation. For example statefulset is expected to have 3 replicas, but it has less than that for a noticeable period of time. In…

rules.title: Kube StatefulSet Update Not RolledOut
rules.summary: StatefulSet update has not been rolled out.

rules.title: Kube Version Mismatch
rules.summary: Different semantic versions of Kubernetes components running. Usually happens during kubernetes cluster upgrade process. Full context Kubernetes control plane nodes or worker nodes use different versions. This usually happens when kubernetes cluster is upgraded between minor and major version.

rules.title: Kubelet Client Certificate Expiration
rules.summary: Client certificate for Kubelet on node expires soon or already expired.

rules.title: Kubelet Client Certificate Renewal Errors
rules.summary: Kubelet on node has failed to renew its client certificate (XX errors in the last 15 minutes)

rules.title: Kubelet Down
rules.summary: This alert is triggered when the monitoring system has not been able to reach any of the cluster's Kubelets for more than 15 minutes.

rules.title: Kubelet Pod Lifecycle Event Generator Duration High
rules.summary: The Kubelet Pod Lifecycle Event Generator has a 99th percentile duration of XX seconds on node.

rules.title: Kubelet Pod Start Up Latency High
rules.summary: Kubelet Pod startup 99th percentile latency is XX seconds on node.

rules.title: Kubelet Server Certificate Expiration
rules.summary: Server certificate for Kubelet on node expires soon or already expired.

rules.title: Kubelet Server Certificate Renewal Errors
rules.summary: Kubelet on node has failed to renew its server certificate (XX errors in the last 5 minutes)

rules.title: Kubelet Too Many Pods
rules.summary: The alert fires when a specific node is running >95% of its capacity of pods (110 by default). Full context Kubelets have a configuration that limits how many Pods they can run. The default value of this is 110 Pods per Kubelet, but it is configurable (and this alert takes that configuration…

rules.title: KubeProxy Down
rules.summary: The KubeProxyDown alert is triggered when all Kubernetes Proxy instances have not been reachable by the monitoring system for more than 15 minutes.

rules.title: Node Clock Not Synchronising
rules.summary: Clock not synchronising.

rules.title: Node Clock Skew Detected
rules.summary: Clock skew detected.

rules.title: Node File Descriptor Limit
rules.summary: This alert is triggered when a node's kernel is found to be running out of available file descriptors -- a warning level alert at greater than 70% usage and a critical level alert at greater than 90% usage.

rules.title: Node Filesystem Almost Out Of Files
rules.summary: This alert is similar to the NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp alert, but rather than being based on a prediction that a filesystem will run out of inodes in a certain amount of time, it uses simple static thresholds. The alert will fire as at a warning level at 5% of available inodes left, and at a…

rules.title: Node Filesystem Almost Out Of Space
rules.summary: This alert is similar to the NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp alert, but rather than being based on a prediction that a filesystem will become full in a certain amount of time, it uses simple static thresholds. The alert will fire as at a warning level at 5% space left, and at a critical level with…

rules.title: Node Filesystem Files Filling Up
rules.summary: This alert is similar to the NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp alert, but predicts the filesystem will run out of inodes rather than bytes of storage space. The alert fires at a critical level when the filesystem is predicted to run out of available inodes within four hours.

rules.title: Node Filesystem Space Filling Up
rules.summary: This alert is based on an extrapolation of the space used in a file system. It fires if both the current usage is above a certain threshold and the extrapolation predicts to run out of space in a certain time. This is a warning-level alert if that time is less than 24h. It's a critical alert if…

rules.title: Node High Number Conntrack Entries Used
rules.summary: Number of conntrack are getting close to the limit.

rules.title: Node Network Interface Flapping
rules.summary: Network interface is often changing its status

rules.title: Node Network Receive Errors
rules.summary: Network interface is reporting many receive errors.

rules.title: Node Network Transmit Errors
rules.summary: Network interface is reporting many transmit errors.

rules.title: Node RAID Degraded
rules.summary: RAID Array is degraded. This alert is triggered when a node has a storage configuration with RAID array, and the array is reporting as being in a degraded state due to one or more disk failures.

rules.title: Node RAID Disk Failure
rules.summary: Runbook guidance for Node RAID Disk Failure.

rules.title: Node Text File Collector Scrape Error
rules.summary: Node Exporter text file collector failed to scrape.

rules.title: Prometheus Missing Rule Evaluations

rules.summary: Prometheus is not connected to any Alertmanagers.

rules.title: Prometheus Not Ingesting Samples
rules.summary: Prometheus is not ingesting samples.

rules.title: Prometheus Operator Node Lookup Errors
rules.summary: Errors while reconciling information about kubernetes nodes.

rules.title: Prometheus Operator NotReady
rules.summary: Prometheus operator is not ready.

rules.title: Prometheus Operator Reconcile Errors
rules.summary: Errors while reconciling controller.

rules.title: Watchdog
rules.summary: This is an alert meant to ensure that the entire alerting pipeline is functional. This alert is always firing, therefore it should always be firing in Alertmanager and always fire against a receiver.

tools.name: Falco rules

rules.title: Adding ssh keys to authorized_keys
rules.summary: After gaining access, attackers can modify the authorizedkeys file to maintain persistence on a victim host. Where authorizedkeys files are modified via cloud APIs or command line interfaces, an adversary may achieve privilege escalation on the target virtual machine if they add a key to a…

rules.title: Backdoored library loaded into SSHD (CVE-2024-3094)
rules.summary: This rule detects possible CVE-2024-3094 exploitation when the SSH daemon process loads a vulnerable version of the liblzma library. An attacker could exploit this to interfere with authentication in sshd via systemd, potentially compromising sensitive data or escalating their privileges.

rules.title: Basic Interactive Reconnaissance
rules.summary: This rule detects basic interactive reconnaissance commands that are typically run by unsophisticated attackers or used in internal Red Team exercises. Interactive is defined as a terminal being present (proc.tty != 0). This could be any form of reverse shell or usage of kubectl exec or ssh etc.…

rules.title: BPF Program Not Profiled
rules.summary: BPF is a kernel technology that can be misused for malicious purposes, like "Linux Kernel Module Injection". This rule should be considered an auditing rule to notify you of any unprofiled BPF tools running in your environment. However, it requires customization after profiling your environment.…

rules.title: Change namespace privileges via unshare
rules.summary: Unprivileged users in containers may not have CAPSYSADMIN or other elevated privileges. However, they can use the unshare system call with CLONENEWNS or CLONENEWUSER to create or clone a namespace or user with the necessary privileges to conduct further attacks. It is best practice to block the…

rules.title: Change thread namespace
rules.summary: An attempt to alter the namespace of a process (often performed while creating a container) through the setns syscall. Conversely, the same syscall setns is triggered when an unauthorized attempt is made to break out from the container to the host, for example, when using commands like nsenter…

rules.title: Clear Log Activities
rules.summary: Detect clearing of critical access log files, typically done to erase evidence that could be attributed to an adversary's actions. To effectively customize and operationalize this detection, check for potentially missing log file destinations relevant to your environment, and adjust the profiled…

rules.title: Contact cloud metadata service from container
rules.summary: Detects attempts to communicate with the Cloud Instance Metadata Service from a container. This detection is narrowly focused and might not apply to your environment. In addition, it could generate noise and require fine-tuning.

rules.title: Contact EC2 Instance Metadata Service From Container
rules.summary: Detects attempts to communicate with the EC2 Instance Metadata Service from a container. This detection is narrowly focused and might not apply to your environment. In addition, it could generate noise and require fine-tuning.

rules.title: Contact K8S API Server From Container
rules.summary: Detect attempts to communicate with the K8S API Server from a container by non-profiled users. Kubernetes APIs play a pivotal role in configuring the cluster management lifecycle. Detecting potential unauthorized access to the API server is of utmost importance. Audit your complete…

rules.title: Container Access to Host Sensitive Paths
rules.summary: Detects container processes accessing paths that typically only exist when the host filesystem is mounted into the container (like /host, /rootfs, /hostfs). This may indicate a container escape attempt or a misconfigured volume mount that exposes the host filesystem. Legitimate monitoring or…

rules.title: Container Accessing GPU Device
rules.summary: Detects a container process opening an NVIDIA or AMD GPU or accelerator character device. Opening such a device is required to submit compute work to the hardware, making this a high-signal indicator of GPU cryptojacking when it originates from a workload that is not expected to use…

rules.title: Container Drift Detected (chmod)
rules.summary: Detect new executables created within a container as a result of chmod. While this detection can generate significant noise, chmod usage is frequently linked to dropping and executing malicious implants. The newer rule "Drop and execute new binary in container" provides more precise detection of…

rules.title: Container Drift Detected (open+create)
rules.summary: Detect new executables created within a container as a result of open+create. The newer rule "Drop and execute new binary in container" provides more precise detection of this TTP using unambiguous kernel signals. It is recommended to use the new rule.

rules.title: Container Run as Root User
rules.summary: Container detected running as the root user. This should be taken into account especially when policies disallow containers from running with root user privileges. Note that a root user in containers doesn't inherently possess extensive power, as modern container environments define privileges…

rules.title: Create files below dev
rules.summary: Detect the creation of files under /dev except for authorized device management programs. This can reveal rootkits hiding files in /dev. Additionally, consider the "Execution from /dev/shm" rule. The upstream rule already covers some tuning scenarios that you can further expand upon.

rules.title: Create Hardlink Over Sensitive Files
rules.summary: Detect hardlink created over a curated list of sensitive files or subdirectories under /etc/ or root directories. Can be customized as needed. Refer to further and equivalent guidance within the rule "Read sensitive file untrusted".

rules.title: Create Hidden Files or Directories
rules.summary: Detecting hidden files or directories creation can serve as an auditing rule to track general system changes. Such rules can be noisy and challenging to interpret, particularly if your system frequently undergoes updates. However, careful profiling of your environment can transform this rule…

rules.title: Create Symlink Over Sensitive Files
rules.summary: Detect symlinks created over a curated list of sensitive files or subdirectories under /etc/ or root directories. Can be customized as needed. Refer to further and equivalent guidance within the rule "Read sensitive file untrusted".

rules.title: DB program spawned process
rules.summary: A program related to the database server creates an unexpected child process (other than itself). This is not supposed to happen and often follows SQL injection attacks. This behavioral detection could indicate potential unauthorized data extraction or tampering with the database.

rules.title: Debugfs Launched in Privileged Container
rules.summary: Detect file system debugger debugfs launched inside a privileged container which might lead to container escape. This rule has a more narrow scope.

rules.title: Decoding Payload in Container
rules.summary: Detect any use of {base64} decoding in a container. Legitimate applications may decode encoded payloads. The template list knowndecodepayloadcontainers can be used for simple tuning and customization, or you can adopt custom, more refined tuning. Less sophisticated adversaries may…

rules.title: Delete or rename shell history
rules.summary: Detect shell history deletion, frequently used by unsophisticated adversaries to eliminate evidence. Note that it can also trigger when exiting a Terminal shell, such as with kubectl exec, which may introduce some noise.

rules.title: Detect crypto miners using the Stratum protocol
rules.summary: Miners commonly specify the mining pool to connect to using a URI that starts with "stratum+tcp". However, this rule is highly specific to this technique, and matching command-line arguments can generally be bypassed quite easily.

rules.title: Detect outbound connections to common miner pool ports
rules.summary: Miners usually connect to miner pools using standard ports, and this rule flags such activity. Important: Falco currently sends DNS requests to resolve miner pool domains, which could trigger other alerts. Prior to enabling this rule, it's advised to ensure whether this is acceptable for your…

rules.title: Detect release_agent File Container Escapes
rules.summary: Detect an attempt to exploit a container escape using releaseagent file. By running a container with certains capabilities, a privileged user can modify releaseagent file and escape from the container.

rules.title: Directory traversal monitored file read
rules.summary: Web applications can be vulnerable to directory traversal attacks that allow accessing files outside of the web app's root directory (e.g. Arbitrary File Read bugs). System directories like /etc are typically accessed via absolute paths. Access patterns outside of this (here path traversal) can…

rules.title: Disallowed SSH Connection Non Standard Port
rules.summary: Detect any new outbound SSH connection from the host or container using a non-standard port. This rule holds the potential to detect a family of reverse shells that cause the victim machine to connect back out over SSH, with STDIN piped from the SSH connection to a shell's STDIN, and STDOUT of…

rules.title: Drop and execute new binary in container
rules.summary: Detect if an executable not belonging to the base image of a container is being executed. The drop and execute pattern can be observed very often after an attacker gained an initial foothold. isexeupperlayer filter field only applies for container runtimes that use overlayfs as union mount…

rules.title: Execution from /dev/shm
rules.summary: This rule detects file execution in the /dev/shm directory, a tactic often used by threat actors to store their readable, writable, and occasionally executable files. /dev/shm acts as a link to the host or other containers, creating vulnerabilities for their compromise as well. Notably, /dev/shm…

rules.title: Exfiltrating Artifacts via Kubernetes Control Plane
rules.summary: Detect the copying of artifacts from a container's file system using the Kubernetes control plane (kubectl cp). This rule can identify potential exfiltration of application secrets from containers' file systems, potentially revealing the outcomes of unauthorized access and control plane misuse…

rules.title: Fileless execution via memfd_create
rules.summary: Detect if a binary is executed from memory using the memfdcreate technique. This is a well-known defense evasion technique for executing malware on a victim machine without storing the payload on disk and to avoid leaving traces about what has been executed. rules.title: Find AWS Credentials
rules.summary: Detect attempts to search for private keys or passwords using the grep or find command, particularly targeting standard AWS credential locations. This is often seen with unsophisticated attackers, as there are many ways to access files using bash built-ins that could go unnoticed. Regardless,…

rules.title: GPU Management Tool Run in Container
rules.summary: Detects execution of an NVIDIA or AMD GPU management or query tool, such as nvidia-smi or rocm-smi, inside a container. Attackers commonly run these tools immediately after gaining access to a GPU-equipped node to fingerprint the available accelerators before deploying a miner. Inside a workload…

rules.title: Interpreted procs inbound network activity
rules.summary: Any inbound network activity performed by any interpreted program (perl, python, ruby, etc.). While it offers broad coverage and behavioral insights, operationalizing it effectively requires significant time and might result in a moderate level of noise. tools.extraction_method: Parsed rule entries from stable, incubating, and sandbox rules YAML.
tools.inventory_caveat: Maturity, exceptions, engine, plugin, and host context determine applicability.

methodology.inventory_unit: One pinned native unit or explicitly derived source artifact per row.
methodology.semantic_grouping: Conservative tool-local grouping for repeated reasons, names, handlers, or normalized check text; groups require human review before scenario mapping.
methodology.derived_id_algorithm: Namespaced tool ID plus a human-readable semantic slug and the first 12 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over the source identity.
methodology.reproducibility: Source revisions and extraction methods are recorded, but the cross-repository extractor is not yet repository-owned; treat this snapshot as provisional.
